title: What would make the bank better off?
opening:
Consider a deposit offer to a defined group of households. The bank can send
the offer or leave its current terms unchanged. For household $i$, let
$C_i(1)$ be contribution over the following year if the offer is assigned and
$C_i(0)$ contribution over that same year under the alternative. Contribution
includes the agreed funding value, interest expense and servicing costs.
Assignment, delivery, acceptance and the resulting price are distinguished
in Chapter~\ref{rewrite:deposit}. The average as
ending:
The scientific and investment questions meet at the same point: whether a
better-supported decision is worth its cost. The chapters that follow supply
the causal arguments, statistical methods, software comparisons and evidence
needed to make that judgment.

title: From an offer effect to annual contribution
opening:
Here the constructed design makes a narrower intervention explicit. Every
assigned offer is delivered, and assignment automatically reprices the eligible
balance for one year. Thus $R=Z$ and the price rule is $r=r_0+Z\Delta r$;
acceptance does not gate the payment. A voluntary activation campaign would
need a different expense equation. Assume no interference across households,
no lost outcomes, and unchanged funding margin and direct cost. If the
expected no-offer balance is $B_0$, the incremen
ending:
For the offer study, the next source of information is assignment support and
correct household aggregation; for the institutional panel it is a coherent
exposure and outcome history. A bank cannot substitute a successful estimate
in one of these populations for the missing design evidence in the other.
The shared report can preserve both questions without pretending they have
the same estimator or sampling law.

title: Servicing decisions change the next decision's information
opening:
A servicing policy chooses whether to contact a borrower at two dates. Let
$A_0,A_1$ be contact decisions, $L_0$ baseline borrower state and $L_1$ the
state observed between contacts. For this constructed example, $Y$ is
gross contribution in pounds over the two-period horizon, excluding contact
cost. The policy comparison is sustained contact versus no contact, not
the regression coefficient of one contact conditional on every later event.
ending:
The financial interpretation follows the reward definition. Where costs are
already subtracted, subtracting contact cost again would double-count it.
Where a bank's reward law and initial distribution must also be estimated,
the supplied-law components of the generated comparison cannot be treated
as known. Outcome follow-up, action support and measured decision history
therefore determine whether its narrower uncertainty can be useful.

title: A learned graph can leave the pricing decision unresolved
opening:
Suppose $X$ measures a proposed rate change in percentage points, $M$ an
intermediate market quantity and $Y$ gross funding contribution in thousands
of pounds. The units and coefficients in this section are authored for the
example. Consider the centered Gaussian observational covariance
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0.6&0.48\\0.6&1.36&1.088\\0.48&1.088&1.8704
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The law satisfies $X\perp Y\mid M$. A chain $X\to M\to Y$, a
fork $X\leftarrow M\to Y$, and a reverse chain $X\leftar
ending:
This is a developed restricted construction, not an executed general
bank-discovery pipeline. The maintained graph family, scalar lag and
innovation law must be defensible before applying it. An unrestricted latent
model may leave the whole line admissible. In the opening pricing example,
the narrower set already contains opposite net values, so a more elaborate
estimator is useful only if its information or restrictions can resolve a
consequential ambiguity. A labelled whole-line result can be the correct
answer to a well-defined question.

title: Correcting records can change the action
opening:
A treatment record is a measurement of an event. Let $A$ be true randomized
receipt, $W$ recorded receipt and $Y$ gross contribution in pounds at a
fixed horizon. In this separate finite example, $P(A=0)=P(A=1)=1/2$
and $\E[Y\mid A=0]=100$, $\E[Y\mid A=1]=140$. Receipt is
randomized by construction; correcting its record would not establish
randomization in an observational campaign.
ending:
al averages
119.1 outcome units in width, compared with about 4.1 for the fuzzy analysis.
The extra width prices justified ignorance. The corruption budget and outcome
support are external premises, not quantities learned from matching confidence.
A monetary decision first maps those outcome units and bounds into its own
expense equation. When the admissible set straddles that decision threshold,
an independently resolved audit sample can be more valuable than a forced
match. The detailed history and audit studies retain the further complications
of dependent records and uncertain audit truth.

title: Constructing a causal model and identifying its questions
opening:
The annual repricing example distinguished assignment from receipt. This
chapter uses a separate ninety-day activation example to show what changes
when customers choose whether to take up an invitation. Its outcome and
action symbols are local to that example.
ending:
The initial product can implement explicit DAG back-door checks and
registered functional templates with human-supplied assumptions. It should
record variable meanings, graph version, intervention transformation,
required kernels, support restrictions and target population weights.
Discovery and automated data preparation can propose inputs to this
process; they cannot certify the absence of unmeasured causes. The next
chapter shows why an instrumental-variable route changes the returned
object even when it uses the same customers, actions and outcomes.

title: From a causal diagram to instrumental-variable estimation
opening:
The graph alone does not generally identify $\E[Y(1)-Y(0)]$
\citep[Section 3.5]{pearl2009}. Linear homogeneous effects, monotone
binary compliance, and a nonparametric structural response each add
different restrictions. This chapter develops the first two and connects
them to the inverse problem that arises in the third. Calling all three
outputs an ``IV effect'' would lose the scientific distinction.
ending:
Each result must carry the original intervention, population, assumptions,
first-stage evidence, score or likelihood, dependence unit and uncertainty
method. A weak first stage should affect the inference state; a disputed
exclusion should affect the causal assumption state. Combining them into
one opaque confidence score would conceal which remedy is required.
Additional randomization can improve support; a different encouragement
may improve relevance; measuring an omitted mechanism may alter the graph.
None of these changes is equivalent to running a more accurate predictor.

title: Identification, statistical efficiency and machine learning
opening:
Suppose Chapter~\ref{r3:graphs} has justified adjustment by $X$. The
observed data for an independent household are $O=(X,A,Y)$, with binary
$A$, propensity $e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)$ and response surfaces
$m_a(x)=\E[Y\mid A=a,X=x]$. The scientific target is the population
average $\theta=\E[m_1(X)-m_0(X)]$, or the conditional contrast
$\tau(x)=m_1(x)-m_0(x)$. These are causal targets only under the
identification assumptions. The same formulas remain statistical
association functionals when those as
ending:
nd support, score stability, fold leakage, local moment rank,
regularization sensitivity and policy-selection rules. Predictive
validation is useful for nuisance fit; it cannot certify exchangeability,
instrument exclusion, causal representation or transport to another bank.
These distinctions also determine what automated data organization is
allowed to discard or aggregate. The next chapter develops inverse
learning with endogeneity and proxies. Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal}
then makes the information set dynamic and shows why sequence prediction
is still only one part of the causal problem.

title: Learning with endogeneity: inverse problems and proxy bridges
opening:
The invitation experiment may identify a linear coefficient or a complier
mean. A bank asking how funding contribution changes over a continuum of
deposit prices poses a different question. Prices can respond to latent
liquidity demand, so a flexible regression of contribution on price learns
the historical conditional mean, not automatically the structural response.
Equation~\eqref{r3:npiv-operator} instead uses an exclusion and conditional
moment to turn that response into an inverse problem.
ending:
A decision changes the information available for the next one. Repeated
contacts, loan modifications and deposit offers therefore require a comparison
of policies over time. Panel and time-series designs add the common shocks
and selection problems faced by banks changing policy across branches or dates.

title: Longitudinal interventions, state estimation and policy value
opening:
A household's liquidity changes after an offer, its updated balance
influences the next offer, and both affect later funding contribution.
Collections has the same feedback: assistance changes arrears, arrears
affect subsequent assistance, and both determine repayment. The model
must preserve which information was available before each action.

title: Changing policies, censoring and events that end a decision
opening:
The history g-formula identifies a specified intervention, not every
quantity labeled a policy effect. A bank may increase an existing offer
probability, modify an employee's proposed credit limit, or stop making
decisions after repayment. These operations use different information
and produce different statistical functionals. Their distinctions also
determine which nuisance functions enter an influence function.
ending:
These distinctions specify the operations a longitudinal product must
accept. An action policy, a natural-action modification, an
observation intervention and an event-removal hypothetical are separate
scientific inputs. An interface that records only an outcome column,
an action column and a horizon cannot distinguish their estimands.

title: Controlled-state identification, estimation and customer choice
opening:
The likelihood and policy-replacement recursions in
Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal} leave an identification question open.
Which controlled transition, reward and observation kernels can the
recorded law determine? The answer depends on who sees the state,
how actions are assigned, what is measured, and which actions the target
policy will use. A repayment trajectory can identify a useful predictive
state without identifying the effect of an untried restructuring.
ending:
This supplies an identified and executed nonlinear reference, including a
useful larger-audit regime and explicit failures. It does not establish
routine validity for arbitrary private-state laws, erroneous audits, weak
information, unrestricted policies or unknown global optimizer behavior.
Those require renewed scientific arguments and evidence.

title: Repeated decisions and customers who disappear
opening:
A servicing policy changes what happens next. A reminder, payment holiday or
collection action affects both the customer's state and the information the
bank subsequently observes. Estimating a policy from customers who remain in
the records can therefore answer a different question from the one the bank
faces. The relevant value averages over the initial eligible population,
including customers whose later outcomes are missing.
ending:
The software implication is concrete. Preserve the initial denominator,
reward-specific weights, information dates and policy-selection split; show
effective information and sensitivity alongside the effect. A commercial or
open-source implementation should be compared on these same meanings. A
successfully executed policy-value calculation does not settle the scientific
conditions that make it useful. Here the next experiment should test those
conditions before seeking a costly bank pilot.

title: A narrower policy interval can be more confidently wrong
opening:
The servicing example leaves a natural question. If a fitted transition
model uses the observed histories more efficiently than weighting, can it
give an informative interval for the gain from intervention? The answer
depends on why outcomes are missing and whether the state equation is
adequate. Resampling quantifies variation in an estimated model; it does
not establish the model's economic assumptions.
ending:
The calculation supports a conditional use of model-based precision and a
clear reason to test the observation and state assumptions before relying
on it. An outcome audit, better follow-up or a richer measured history can
change those assumptions' credibility. More bootstrap draws alone cannot.
These results remain a generated research comparison with known reward
and initial laws; a bank application needs its own economic specification,
sampling argument and measurement evidence.

title: Panel data: heterogeneity, timing and structural moments
opening:
A panel of branch deposits can support several different questions.
One can model a homogeneous response to price after removing stable
branch differences, identify an adoption-cohort effect from untreated
trends, fit an interactive-factor counterfactual, or estimate a dynamic
equation using lagged instruments. All use a rectangular data set;
their counterfactual assumptions are different.
ending:
r stability plus a stationary exponentially mixing data law.
These are substantive ways to trade assignment information for temporal
prediction restrictions. Neither is a license to permute arbitrary
nonstationary bank residuals, and neither automatically changes a sharp
path hypothesis into the mean effect in Equation~\eqref{s6:aggregate-att-if}.
For an observational regional rollout this challenger can be selected only
after its null prediction and temporal restrictions are defended. The
randomized pilot route was selected here because its source of repeated
assignment is specified directly.

title: When a bank in the data ceases to be the same bank
opening:
A funding study follows institutions through time. Its economic interpretation
requires the deposit outcome and the exposure to refer to the same institution.
A fixed effect removes a persistent level difference; it cannot repair an outcome
assigned to the wrong institution. This distinction matters before a bank spends
money on a more elaborate covariance estimator.
ending:
The calculation was checked against an explicit regression with institution
and date indicator variables. Coefficients and all three covariance formulas
agree to better than $10^{-10}$ on the independent small-panel check. This
supports the reported arithmetic. It does not validate an unobserved bank's
history, guarantee finite-panel coverage, or establish a preferred estimator
outside the specified cases.

title: Time series, structural shocks and observation frequency
opening:
In treasury and deposit management, a bank may ask how a policy-rate
shock changes balances over the next year. In collections it may ask
how repeated assistance changes repayment along a customer trajectory.
Both have time indices, but the interventions differ. A structural
macroeconomic shock perturbs one innovation while the system's other
mechanisms continue to respond. A sustained policy replaces a sequence
of decision rules. A forecast conditions on observed historical values.
These are di
ending:
A bank can therefore reuse this selected learning route with an explicit
dictionary, causal information and rate argument. It cannot substitute a
different learner on the strength of a common method signature. Nor can the
independent-pair audit result be attached to this calendar score without a
joint sampling derivation.

title: Continuous time, observation events and structural dynamics
opening:
A credit line can change on a decision date, a payment can arrive at any
instant, and a financial statement can be entered weeks after the period
it describes. Putting all three on a monthly grid is a modeling choice.
The event clock in Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal} must extend to continuous
time without confusing a changing customer state, the times at which the
bank observes it, and the times at which the bank acts.
ending:
The computational contract includes continuous dynamics, action and
observation clocks, event marks, time units, the sampling operator and
information available to each policy. An ODE/SDE solver, event likelihood
and causal identification procedure solve different parts of that contract.
Their numerical success must remain separate from evidence for its
structural assumptions.

title: Learning decisions and designing their evidence
opening:
An estimated causal response is an input to a decision problem. The
bank must specify which decisions it can change, which resources they
consume and whose value is averaged. Selecting a policy also changes
the statistical problem: the selected rule is random, and its empirical
value benefits from the same noise that made it win.
ending:
A large dataset can leave the causal question unresolved. Several mechanisms
may explain the same correlations, customer histories may be linked incorrectly,
and a result from one population may fail in another. These limits determine
which assumptions to defend and which additional information to seek.

title: Discovery, graph uncertainty and identification across models
opening:
A bank might supply monthly balances, offered rates, accepted products,
customer contacts and arrears to a discovery procedure. A graph over these
columns is not yet a graph over economic mechanisms. The offer precedes
acceptance, balances are stocks measured at particular dates, arrears affect
eligibility, and a relationship manager may use private information. The
same table can therefore be compatible with several latent-variable and
observation models. The variables, information dates and in
ending:
The supplied-sufficiency interval relaxation is sometimes extremely wide,
including whole-line output in most draws of one sufficient design. Accidental
coverage under a false premise is not evidence for that premise. The omitted
prior-path stress arm represents an exclusion failure through its reduced-form
direct path; a full dependent-history extension remains separate. This selected
construction consequently closes a bounded observation-law-to-effect argument,
while useful arbitrary learned-PAG confidence and scalable sharp optimization
remain open.

title: Observation processes and automatic organization of banking data
opening:
Useful automation instead makes the observation assumptions explicit,
checks their observable implications and preserves information for an
appropriate estimator. The aim is to automate reproducible construction
of an analysis view while retaining a scientific record of what that view
means. Data lineage proves how a variable was computed; it does not prove
that the variable blocks a confounding path.
ending:
The practical alternatives are consequently clear. Use the original rectangle
when preserving disconnected topology matters; use the registered ellipsoid
when covariance is well qualified and its outer interval is suitable; retain
the regular calculation as a disclosed research route; or purchase the
outcome-linked information in Section~\ref{c7:persistent-audits}. None may be
selected after observing which produces the narrowest favorable answer.

title: An uncertain customer identity changes the economic question
opening:
A customer table and an outcome table do not become one economic sample merely
because a matching algorithm returns a name. A wrong match assigns somebody
else's outcome to the intervention. An unmatched record removes an outcome
from the comparison. These are different errors, and either can change the
case for spending.
ending:
The economically useful repair is to narrow justified uncertainty: improve
record identity, validate a tighter outcome range, or audit enough links to
defend a smaller exclusion budget. Forcing every customer to one outcome
merely conceals the information problem. An analysis that cannot support a
spending decision can still show which information is worth buying.

title: Transport, invariance and sensitivity across bank environments
opening:
An estimate that is credible in one market may be misleading in another,
even when the same statistical method is applied correctly.
Product eligibility, customer composition, competitive responses and
measurement systems can all change. The relevant question is which
parts of a causal model remain invariant, and which target-domain
information can replace the parts that do not.
ending:
ly, transport to a future market combines causal invariance
with uncertainty about the future environment. A forecast of future
covariate distributions is not an observed target law. Large-scale
adoption may itself change competitor prices, customer choices and
funding costs, so that the environment depends on the policy. Such
equilibrium effects need a structural market model or a design with
variation at the relevant market scale. Historical invariance tests
and account-level causal estimates can inform that model but cannot
identify the resulting equilibrium merely by being pooled together.

title: Sensitivity when the identifying assumptions are uncertain
opening:
The preceding estimators are conditional conclusions: given the
stated graph, moment restrictions, support and observation process,
they estimate a specified causal functional. A bank rarely knows
those premises with certainty. Sensitivity analysis should therefore
describe an explicit larger model class and propagate its ambiguity
to the financial target. Replacing one flexible regression by another
mostly probes estimation choices; it does not probe the omitted
mechanisms those regressions sha
ending:
he causal model class. Their
combination must be defined jointly; independently varying several
knobs and taking the largest separate effect need not bound their
combined effect. A policy recommendation can be robust across a
declared ambiguity set, or conditional on one defended model. Neither
label should hide how that model or set was chosen.
For the linkage problem, Section~\ref{s61:linkage-sets} executes this
confidence-region inclusion argument through a finite interval-union
algorithm. Its full-line results also show why coverage and decision
informativeness must be reported separately.

title: What recent learning methods change, and what they inherit
opening:
The preceding chapters distinguish the intervention, identification functional,
statistical experiment and numerical method. This distinction provides a way
to read the current literature without equating architectural novelty with a
new identification result. A transformer can estimate a conditional law, an
orthogonal learner can estimate a moment, and a simulator can integrate a
g-formula. They solve different parts of the same argument. For the bank,
the useful comparison is the scientific wo
ending:
The journeys and their foundations determine what a useful service must
preserve. These chapters bring software selection, assistance, public
evidence and implemented interfaces into that argument. Detailed comparisons
then develop the individual methods. The final investment part uses their
results and limitations to price the next experiment.

title: Choosing the capabilities worth assembling
opening:
A bank does not buy an average treatment effect. It buys a better decision:
which customers to contact, which price to quote, which branches to reorganise,
or which experiment to fund. Software is useful when its answer bears on that
decision and its assumptions are credible in the setting. A method that answers
a narrower question accurately can be more valuable than an ambitious system
whose output is difficult to interpret.
ending:
Some limits require new information rather than more programming: unidentified
effects under unrestricted confounding, absent support for a proposed action,
unknown assignment histories and uncertain transfer to a new population. State
the restrictions or data that would narrow each limit. These findings can
support a useful proposal even when they do not support a universal product.

title: Which tasks merit language assistance?
opening:
Assistance should be selected by the task it improves. A system that answers
questions about a supplied causal mechanism has not thereby shown that
it can discover a defensible mechanism for a new bank. The evidence
synthesis in Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} and the detailed studies
support a restricted comparison, with a questionnaire and ordinary search
as serious alternatives. They do not establish a measured saving for this
proposed product.
ending:
trieval and explicit alternatives, evaluated against
the questionnaire. Identification and numerical results remain delegated
to defined procedures. Expansion to autonomous discovery, variable
construction or recommendations requires task-specific evidence. The
frontier evidence includes the three additional inspected originals discussed
in Section~\ref{gap29:frontier}. The current census is 85 inspected and
28 unread; these omissions still limit broad claims. A live comparison still
requires a fixed model version, held-out questions, matched information,
independent adjudication and a budget.

title: When a statistical difference changes a banking decision
opening:
The case for a shared analytical service is strongest when it prevents a
material mistake, exposes a valuable uncertainty or makes a defensible study
less costly. The following examples examine those propositions directly.
They are project-generated calculations, not measurements of bank returns or
claims of superiority over an installed commercial system. A fixed design
specifies the scenarios and comparisons before the simulation is run.
ending:
The practical implication is observable without private bank data. A common
study interface should record which variables exist at the action date and
which records support the claimed evaluation. A simple rule excluding duration
already prevents one misleading improvement. Language assistance would need
to outperform that rule or uncover a harder omission to justify its extra
cost. The next experiment should compare completed analyst studies with these
requirements enforced, rather than rewarding the largest retrospective score.

title: What a public experiment can tell a bank
opening:
A useful prototype should take an intervention question through to a decision
that an economist can defend. Public data permits that exercise before a bank
commits staff time, customer records and money to a pilot. Its value depends on
which question it answers. A public experiment can test whether an analysis
preserves the population, intervention and uncertainty. It cannot establish
that the same intervention works for a bank's customers.
ending:
Marking the assignment premise contradicted produces a refusal. Keeping it
unverified preserves conditional inference rather than certifying truth.
These behaviours make the worked example useful to an economist: uncertainty
and missing evidence survive the change of interface. They do not qualify a
bank platform or a sibling repository.

title: A shared service for economic analysis
opening:
A banking study connects a feasible action to its financial consequence
through a defensible account of customer behaviour. The underlying event
records have changing identities and reporting delays. An economist supplies restrictions on
assignment or shocks; a learner estimates conditional distributions; a
validator needs a sampling argument; a decision maker needs the value of
a feasible policy. A shared product is useful when it preserves the
meaning of the question across those transformatio
ending:
Direct expert composition can call the same qualified kernels and satisfy the
same unit, provenance, uncertainty and reporting obligations. The shared product
is valuable only if it helps preserve those obligations across repeated tasks.
The local matched computation compares identical public output bytes; it does
not measure analyst savings or establish acceptance by FinMarketing,
BayesFilter, MacroFinance or dataml. Their inspected interfaces remain concrete
integration proposals until their owners qualify and adopt the mappings.

title: What the local study interfaces preserve
opening:
An illustrative economist asks about the twelve-month value of an offer among
eligible accounts. The supplied diagram contains an arrow from offer to value,
and the sampling assumption is independent accounts. That diagram is explicitly
unverified. The local walkthrough sends the same question through the Python
library, a command-line process and a local MCP client. It exercises the
repository's existing implementation; it does not connect another repository,
invoke a language model or fit an e
ending:
The economic comparison of these workflows is developed in
Chapter~\ref{rewrite:investment-decision}. Its account includes unsuccessful
studies, correction, interpretation and maintenance, and distinguishes a
prototype comparison from a later bank-data pilot.

title: What the evidence changes about the proposed service
opening:
The four journeys distinguish a wrong target, insufficient treatment support,
causal ambiguity and uncertain measurement. Those failures demand different
responses. A common service should make the distinctions visible while
reusing the appropriate statistical procedures. Its initial scope follows
from the evidence below; it does not require every possible capability to
be implemented at once.
ending:
Software is useful when its methods answer the economic question under
credible assumptions. The comparisons begin with the relationships that a
method can discover and the effects it can identify. They distinguish a supplied
causal model from one learned from data and compare alternatives across languages.

title: What a shared service must preserve
opening:
The preceding theory makes software selection more demanding than choosing
an estimator with an attractive name. A deposit-retention analysis may ask
for an average effect across customers, across branches, or across balances.
A collections analysis may ask for an effect of a fixed schedule, a rule
using available history, or a modification of the historical assignment
law. These distinctions change the estimand before any package is called.
The common product needs to preserve them as it moves
ending:
An expert team can compose the same open-source libraries directly.
The shared product has value only if it preserves the scientific contracts
more reliably, reduces repeated data and validation work, and improves
decision throughput at a measured total cost. An estimator wrapper with
a common name adds little. The operations, invalid requests, numerical
obligations and reusable artifacts in Chapter~\ref{r3:product} make this
claim testable. The comparisons here explain why those requirements follow
from the economic question, rather than from a preference for a particular
software interface.

title: Choosing software by the economic question
opening:
A bank considering a causal library faces several different purchasing and
engineering decisions. It may need a defensible effect of an invitation, a
description of plausible causal directions among funding variables, or a
policy for repeated servicing decisions. A package that produces a directed
graph does not necessarily answer the first question. A package that estimates
an average treatment effect does not necessarily answer the third. The survey
therefore takes a scientific operation as it
ending:
and
future maintenance. A free download can still require expensive scientific
adaptation; an enterprise license can be worthwhile if its documented service
and measured workflow fit the request. Before paying for a trial, the proposal
can identify the unresolved comparison and calculate the decision threshold
at which its answer matters. The next expense then purchases information
about a specific choice. The present source survey supplies candidate paths
and testable restrictions; the proposed matched trial supplies the evidence
needed to choose among them.
\label{exec13:survey-reviewed-end}

title: Comparing methods by what they estimate
opening:
A bank does not need an abstract winner among causal libraries. It needs to
know whether a particular computation answers its particular question. A
funding desk might ask how changing a quoted rate affects twelve-month retained
balances. A servicing team might ask when to contact an account whose financial
condition changes after earlier contacts. A model-risk team might ask whether
two plausible causal diagrams imply different intervention decisions. These
questions require different informati
ending:
The initial adoption preference is therefore to evaluate the existing Java
engine through a narrow process boundary, with endpoint roundtrips and typed
failure handling. Porting an isolated helper would omit the graph semantics
that make its output meaningful. For aGrUM, the existing C++ core and Python
wrapper deserve comparison before any reimplementation. Its saved build files
declare version 3.2.0 and C++20; these are environment requirements to test,
not evidence that the proposed binary or wrapper already works.

title: Discovery across independent, latent, temporal and experimental settings
opening:
A bank may want a causal diagram for several quite different reasons. It may
need to identify an adjustment set for an offer, investigate whether a funding
relationship survives a policy change, or decide which experiment would resolve
an ambiguity that matters financially. These uses do not imply the same
learning problem. A discovery engine can be useful while leaving the effect
unresolved; it can also orient more edges under assumptions that the bank has
no reason to accept. The proposal ther
ending:
It must retain
all requests, budget exits and graph ambiguities; compare FCI, RFCI and FCI+
on the same declared laws; and separate native numerical behavior from
serialization correctness. Endpoint pairs, isolated nodes, invalid graph
types, column permutations, diagnostic completeness and search truncation
need individual fixtures. Only after those results should a decision study
evaluate whether a justified effect or refusal changes contact policy value.
No package execution, finite-sample calibration or accepted R adapter is
claimed by the present source review.
\label{exec13:latent-r-end}

title: Learning a causal model from observational data
opening:
A discovery method can narrow the plausible economic relationships without
settling the effect of a proposed action. The comparisons here follow that
remaining question through specific implementation choices. A supplied graph
can support a checked adjustment candidate; a learned structural model adds
assumptions about functions and disturbances; hidden borrower circumstances
change the graph information that must be retained. The practical choice
depends on those assumptions as well as the comp
ending:
Public fixtures can test the proposed worker before costly bank experiments.
They cannot certify an unknown business graph, create unobserved causes
or supply a universal dependence correction. Selected static, temporal,
latent and nonlinear families require their own qualification. Execution and independent validation remain outstanding.
\citep{exec24_lingam_choice}

title: From a learned graph to a defensible calculation
opening:
A graph becomes useful to a bank when its statistical meaning survives
the next calculation. Directed, partially directed and mixed graphs encode
different information. The Tetrad bridge comparison first follows variable
identity, categories and endpoint marks across languages. Weka and Banjo then
show why a predictive factorization or a lagged search still needs a separate
intervention argument. The remaining studies examine calculations under a
supplied model: libDAI distinguishes conditioning
ending:
ntly
successful but unusable answer. A bridge can change variable meaning, a
predictor can answer a conditional rather than interventional question, and
an inference engine can solve the wrong numerical objective. Even the right
objective may have unsupported probability terms or an inadequate numerical
approximation. The shared service must preserve the question at each of
these steps. The authoritative software choice in
Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software} therefore remains selective reuse with explicit
scientific and numerical boundaries; these examples explain the obligations
behind that choice.

title: Learning relationships over time
opening:
A funding decision has a date, an information set and an outcome horizon.
A learned temporal relationship has these attributes only if the observation
and estimation procedure preserve them. Yesterday's rate may predict tomorrow's
balance because the rate changes retention, because both respond to a shared
liquidity shock, or because aggregation conceals their within-day order. The
useful question is what the observed sequence and any intervention information
allow the bank to distinguish.
ending:
stion. Correct row
order does not establish an intervention, a fitted graph does not settle
its unresolved endpoints, and a valid score calculation does not supply a
sampling law. The language and delegate studies show where each distinction
can be preserved or lost. A useful implementation should return the
prediction, graph class, identified effect or refusal that the declared
information supports, together with the uncertainty appropriate to that
object. The next chapter develops the identification and counterfactual
calculations that follow once this information and model have been stated.

title: Identification, counterfactuals and effect sets
opening:
A bank can know that an offer increases average completion and still be unable
to say which completed applications the offer caused. It can identify the
effect of sending an encouragement without identifying the effect of making
every customer receive the service. It can also possess a valid identifying
formula whose numerical evaluation is too fragile to support the proposed
decision. These are different limits on what a causal product can say. The
choice between software components depends on
ending:
ative.
An unidentified individual response, an unsupported graph class, an exhausted
search and a failed numerical calculation have different remedies. The
worked laws also show when an unresolved individual quantity need not block
an average-value decision, and when a harm constraint makes that same
ambiguity decisive. A shared interface earns its value by keeping those
distinctions available to the decision maker. The next two chapters follow
the result into estimating equations and covariance calculations, where
population weights, nuisance fits and dependence introduce further obligations.

title: Functional discovery, symbolic identification and estimating equations
opening:
A bank may ask a single software team to discover a graph, identify an effect
and estimate the value of an offer. Those requests have different outputs.
Discovery can return a selected directed graph, an equivalence class or a set
of candidates. Identification can return an expression in the observed law or
a nonidentification result. Estimation can return a number with a sampling
uncertainty claim. A shared product becomes misleading when it places all
three behind a field named ``causal effect
ending:
l disagreements should be classified by cause before they are ranked.
A different estimand is a semantic mismatch. A failed root solve is a numerical
failure. Nonidentification is a scientific outcome. An unsupported covariance
law is a scope limitation. Timing a successful branch while discarding the
others rewards a system for silently avoiding difficult requests. The full
comparison must retain them and distinguish source inspection from executed
behavior. These distinctions make the software survey useful for design and
investment even when it concludes that a component should be deferred.

title: Keeping causal uncertainty through the calculation
opening:
A funding analyst may represent the offer rate, customer response and retained
balance by three columns in a matrix. The columns are measurements; the graph
and structural equations give those measurements causal meaning. An adapter
must preserve both. A correctly sized matrix can still encode every arrow in
the wrong direction, and a software object called a mixed graph can still
contain a directed cycle that is inadmissible for the requested identification
algorithm. These errors arise before
ending:
An identified effect still needs an estimator, a suitable comparison group
and a defensible account of uncertainty. The choice differs for an invitation,
an eligibility threshold, a repeated servicing rule and a branch rollout.
Commercial and open-source alternatives are assessed against those distinctions.

title: Effect estimation, heterogeneous actions and threshold comparisons
opening:
A servicing team may want to know the value of offering assistance to every
eligible account, the value among accounts already receiving assistance, or
the value in the population where receipt remains uncertain. Those questions
need not have the same answer. Nor does learning a large conditional benefit
identify the best use of a scarce specialist team. A threshold experiment can
support a local comparison while leaving the portfolio decision unresolved.
The proposal therefore needs a vocabular
ending:
iction versus treatment-specific regressions, or a row average versus an
average over customers. The retained numerical witnesses show how such changes
can reverse a financial recommendation even before estimation error is added.
The preferred reference routes therefore remain method-specific, with their
known restrictions and failed cases visible. If conditional exchangeability
cannot be defended, a more flexible learner does not complete the argument.
The next chapter examines what an instrument or eligibility threshold can
identify instead, and which population that information can support.

title: Instruments, eligibility thresholds and the population affected
opening:
An invitation or eligibility rule can create a useful comparison even
when customers choose whether to participate. The effect for customers whose
behaviour changes at that margin need not equal the effect for every customer.
Software choices must respect the instrument, cutoff and population that
supply the identifying information.
ending:
The comparisons support a common decision rule without making the engines
interchangeable. Choose the intervention and affected population first, then
preserve the identifying design, numerical exclusions and actual uncertainty
object. A latent loading, a local receipt effect and the value of changing
eligibility can each be useful, but one cannot stand in for another. The next
chapter draws together the reporting and diagnostic implications before the
argument turns to channels, doses and sensitivity to assumptions.

title: Design-based estimation, weak information and diagnostics
opening:
The preceding comparisons establish why a common interface must preserve
design-specific meanings. This chapter gathers their consequences for the
analyst's report: state the instrument claim, retain the complete uncertainty
set, distinguish threshold designs and show what a sensitivity parameter does
and does not reveal. The detailed implementation findings remain in the
preceding chapter; the purpose here is to connect them to the bank's decision.
ending:
These tools can make a funding or credit recommendation more intelligible:
they expose how much an assumption would need to change before a conclusion
changes. They cannot supply verified instrument exclusion, known ownership,
correct record inclusion or a gold audit label. Their adoption is therefore
conditional on a result contract that separates observed data summaries,
user-supplied sensitivity assumptions and causal conclusions.

title: Channels, doses and sensitivity to assumptions
opening:
A bank may know that a policy works on average and still need to choose
which mechanism to change, how large an intervention to offer and how much
confidence to place in the causal assumptions. These are related decisions,
but they require different targets. We begin with channel attribution and
feasible mediator interventions, then compare natural-effect estimation and
sensitivity methods across implementations. The final dose analysis asks how
to choose an amount rather than merely fit a respo
ending:
The chapter's alternatives therefore turn on what can actually be changed:
an offer, a mediator distribution, an exposure amount or an assumption used
to interpret observations. Natural components, dose optima and sensitivity
thresholds are useful only when their distinct meanings reach the financial
decision. Repeated servicing adds a further requirement: an action changes
information and opportunities for later actions. The next chapter develops
that longitudinal clock and separates policy value, censoring and survival
outcomes before comparing the corresponding software.

title: Longitudinal and survival software as a decision model
opening:
A bank comparing repeated servicing policies needs more than a curve with a
confidence ribbon. An account can default, repay early, cease to be observed,
or receive a different action after its financial condition changes. A policy
that reduces default incidence can also shorten the profitable relationship.
A policy that improves every baseline risk stratum can have a larger late
hazard among its remaining accounts. Two programs can return numerically
similar objects named survival while countin
ending:
The chapter's common requirement is to preserve the same account history
through every stage of the calculation. Changing the time origin, event
priority, policy law, averaging population or unit of uncertainty can change
the financial decision while leaving a plausible curve on the screen. The
mathematical references and source-specific failures show which distinctions
a proposed worker must expose. The next treatment compares regimes,
heterogeneous effects and continuous doses using those requirements, rather
than assuming that one longitudinal label makes the methods interchangeable.

title: Longitudinal regimes, heterogeneous effects and continuous doses
opening:
The detailed comparisons distinguish complete policy evaluation from components
that estimate heterogeneity or a dose curve. This chapter brings those choices
back to a small set of servicing and incentive requests. Its finite examples
show why the same data field or output name cannot determine which component
the bank needs. The preceding source studies supply the implementation limits;
the task here is to preserve them when composing the workflow.
ending:
An eventual selection can combine components: symbolic identification, a
longitudinal engine, a heterogeneous-effect estimator and a dose-response
component can coexist behind one semantic contract. The common contract must
preserve their distinct assumptions and outputs. It should make unsupported
requests explicit rather than coercing every query into the nearest available
estimator.

title: Longitudinal treatment, monitoring and mediation
opening:
Policy choice also determines what the bank observes. Monitoring can change
record availability, and a recorded engagement measure may become a mediator
rather than a baseline control. The compact example here connects these roles
to the detailed longitudinal and mediation comparisons, so that an interface
preserves the question before routing it to an R estimator.
ending:
Porting is an alternative only after the complete method boundary is clear.
Reimplementing a final regression while omitting its expansion, sequential
weighting, model-refitting bootstrap or stopping conditions would create a
different procedure. The advantage of a native port must be demonstrated on
the full workflow, including data transfer, model fitting, uncertainty and
failure handling. A faster final matrix multiplication is not enough.

title: Choosing repeated actions
opening:
A repeated servicing decision changes both cash flows and the information
available for later decisions. Choosing software therefore begins with the
policy question: evaluate a fixed rule from logged experience, learn a rule
and evaluate it separately, or plan within a supplied model. A numerical
answer can be accurate for one of these questions and misleading for another.
ending:
ctions and a stationary population value answer different
questions. The source-specific counterexamples show why state sufficiency,
policy randomness, episode endings, support and reward clocks must survive
conversion. The preferred route is consequently narrow reuse with explicit
qualification and independent finite references; neither a language change nor
a more elaborate optimizer supplies missing causal information. The next
chapter turns to comparisons across institutions and time, where assignment,
shared shocks and the choice of comparison group impose a different set of
requirements.

title: Panel and time-series comparisons for a banking rollout
opening:
A regional rollout of a deposit-servicing program creates several plausible
comparisons. An early region can be compared with a later region, with a
weighted combination of unaffected regions, or with its own forecast under the
old operating rule. Each comparison uses a different source of counterfactual
information. They also answer different questions when treatment effects
vary over the life of a relationship, the donor regions face different funding
shocks, or the bank changes the rule that
ending:
supported populations;
synthetic comparisons require defended donor and calendar information;
feedback analysis requires a specified intervention and stable structural
meaning. A numerical engine can support any of these only through a matching
statistical design. The detailed failures therefore matter alongside the
successful algebra: lost rows, changed weights, substituted intervals and
unreported solver limits can alter the decision. The next chapter develops
trend-sensitivity inference, asking how much confidence the rollout conclusion
warrants when counterfactual trends remain uncertain.

title: How much confidence should a rollout comparison command?
opening:
Branch and customer weights determine whose benefit is being measured;
common shocks determine how much independent information the study contains.
Reported uncertainty must reflect both. The calculations examine changes in
weights, covariance and trend assumptions before interpreting an event-study
coefficient as a reliable financial comparison.
ending:
ts reported interval
must retain the population, sampling law and method that produced it, and its
causal interpretation must withstand the defended counterfactual restrictions.
A reliable conversion cannot supply a missing trend assumption; a sensitivity
analysis cannot repair a lost covariance or a failed numerical bound. When
those obligations leave a wide or disconnected set, the unresolved result is
part of the decision. The next comparison examines how donor construction and
synthetic controls offer different counterfactual information, with their own
extrapolation and uncertainty costs.

title: Synthetic controls and the choice of a comparison
opening:
When one region or institution changes policy, a weighted combination
of unaffected units may offer a comparison. Its usefulness depends on donor
information, pre-intervention fit and the assumptions linking that fit to the
untreated future. The methods differ in how they extrapolate and how they
represent uncertainty; those differences matter for the bank's decision.
ending:
extrapolation; augmentation trades imbalance against model dependence;
factor reconstruction needs informative pre-treatment directions; prediction
intervals must include the uncertainty appropriate to the requested outcome.
The source studies show where those meanings can be lost through weights,
clocks, solver status or selected placebo populations. A good pre-fit curve
alone settles none of these choices. The following synthesis returns them
to population targets, rollout timing and the alternatives available to the
bank, before the later time-series treatment examines changing mechanisms.

title: Panel effects, event studies and synthetic controls
opening:
The preceding chapters developed panel contrasts, event-path uncertainty and
comparison trajectories in detail. This chapter brings their consequences
back to the banking request: whose effect is being estimated, at which event
time, under which comparison law, and with what uncertainty? The examples
below show why a common reporting interface must preserve those distinctions.
The CausalImpact study adds a Bayesian prediction approach whose causal
interpretation depends on an unaffected comparis
ending:
These comparisons concern effects of declared interventions and trajectories
under declared counterfactual laws. A lag coefficient in a dynamic panel or
a response to a structural funding shock requires a further account of
endogeneity and shock identification. The next chapter develops that
additional distinction.

title: Dynamic panels and structural funding shocks
opening:
A deposit response evolves over time and may coincide with changes in
monetary conditions or customer demand. Dynamic-panel moments, restrictions
on structural shocks and state-space forecasts use different sources of
information. A forecast alone does not establish the effect of changing the
bank's policy.
ending:
The funding question can also depend on uncertain customer relationships and
on whether a pilot population represents the intended rollout. The next chapter
extends the information question to relationship graphs, transported policies
and audit design: what additional observations would actually distinguish the
bank's competing decisions?

title: Uncertain relationships, transported policies and the information to audit
opening:
The chapter develops the information needed to move from uncertain customer
relationships to a policy decision in a new population. Exact examples first
separate graph ambiguity, coordinated action, transport and audit design. The
implementation comparisons then ask which parts of that argument survive
linkage, imputation, discovery, historical retrieval and reporting. Repeated
population-weighting and pooling examples provide matched arithmetic checks;
they do not constitute independent evidenc
ending:
A defensible recommendation therefore retains the missing information and its
monetary consequence. It may call for an additional joint audit, a different
allocation, a restricted target population, sensitivity analysis or refusal.
The software choices matter because their score, covariance, mask, clock and
failure behavior can preserve or change that recommendation. The next chapter
examines hidden-state and Bayesian computations as further conditional tools,
with their assumptions carried into the comparison.

title: Hidden states and Bayesian comparisons
opening:
An uncertain customer state can be useful for a banking decision only if its
meaning, observation law and action mechanism are specified. This chapter first
examines state filtering and probabilistic model surgery through Dynamax, PyMC
and NumPyro. It then compares the resulting requirements across languages and
commercial engines. The comparison keeps causal identification, parameter and
state uncertainty, predictive variation and numerical approximation distinct.
Similar finite examples provid
ending:
The next chapter adds another source of dependence: one customer's action can
affect another customer's outcome. A precise individual-state calculation does
not by itself define that allocation problem. The relevant joint policy,
exposure mapping and population must be supplied before comparing its value.

title: Interference, allocation policies and software adoption
opening:
The preceding relationship analysis showed why a policy may require joint
graph and action information. This chapter examines the allocation problem
itself. It distinguishes network and grouped targets, develops the two initial
software references, and compares spatial, experimental, learned-policy and
simulation alternatives. The recurring small graphs and cost denominators are
matched comparison devices; each implementation's different assumptions and
failure conditions remain part of the argu
ending:
The practical choice is conditional reuse of a component whose target and
failure behavior match the banking request, with exact small examples supplying
a first comparison and native trials supplying separate implementation evidence.
The next chapter returns to customer histories, heterogeneity and monetary units,
where the same discipline is needed even when an explicit network is absent.

title: Customer histories, heterogeneous effects and economic units
opening:
This chapter returns to the customer-level request after the network comparisons.
The earlier longitudinal, forest and dose studies supply the detailed methods;
the question here is what must remain unchanged when their outputs are reused.
Whole histories, within-period event order, the population being averaged and
the units of a treatment density can each change the economic answer. The
examples retain those distinctions without treating a common interface as a
common estimand.
ending:
The commercial comparison that follows applies the same criteria to documented
vendor capabilities and to this proposal's actual evidence. A product feature
is useful only for a specified request; a proposed preserving interface is not
yet demonstrated superiority over an existing engine.

title: Commercial alternatives and the capabilities still needed
opening:
A bank does not purchase ``causal inference'' in the abstract. It purchases a
workflow for a named decision, under a named information clock, with a named
population, data owner and loss function. A lending committee might ask whether
an eligibility threshold changes repayment, a treasury desk might ask whether a
rate change changes retained balances, and a servicing team might ask whether a
sequence of contacts is worth its cost. A commercial product can be excellent
for one of these questions
ending:
e cost and capacity derivations apply only after those scientific objects
match. Model residency, online information, deadlines and shared validation
dependencies can change which licensed configuration is useful. Hypothetical
cost crossings and compatibility signals identify measurements that could
change a purchase; they do not establish actual savings. The defensible
recommendation is conditional reuse with a preserving interface and a matched
comparison of the complete workflow. The next chapter develops the
identification and counterfactual distinctions that such an interface must
retain.

title: Commercial identification, counterfactuals and the information a bank must supply
opening:
The preceding chapter made acquisition conditional on preserving the scientific
question. This chapter develops that condition through identification,
counterfactuals, heterogeneity, instruments, event histories and policy value.
It then compares the engine and application boundaries that carry those objects.
The method studies establish the targets and counterexamples; the later
product studies use them to choose a particular interface, entitlement and
qualification path. These are related deci
ending:
ter status, event clocks, selected populations, licenses,
asynchronous failures and cache identity can all change the interpretation
or cost of an otherwise correct calculation. Their implementation-specific
witnesses remain reasons to test a narrow adapter, rather than grounds for a
product-wide ranking. Existing engines supply substantial capabilities; the
proposed common layer earns its place only if the complete comparison shows
that it preserves meaning and improves the accepted workflow. The next
chapter develops the corresponding obligations when computation crosses a
language boundary.

title: Reusing causal software across languages without changing the question
opening:
The commercial comparisons showed that a result can change meaning at an
interface. Here the question is what it takes to preserve a computation across
languages. The argument proceeds from exact branches, shared fits, resampling
and graph identity to numerical composition and conditional path laws. It then
examines retries, persistent failure and selection correction, because the
law of returned results can change even when every completed calculation is
accurate. These derivations determine wh
ending:
e obligations can simplify.
If these premises are unknown, a public-data experiment can test a bounded
profile and estimate diagnostics, while the proposal records the remaining
assumptions. No finite example here establishes universal port equivalence,
qualified dependent-data uncertainty, or a deployed banking service.
The next chapter uses these distinctions to compare build, buy and integration
routes on the same assigned workload and full lifecycle cost. Preserving the
procedure is an admission condition for that comparison, not a conclusion
that a port will be the least expensive choice.

title: Build, buy or combine existing methods?
opening:
Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software} gives the principal software recommendation.
This chapter supplies its comparative decision argument: admission before
price, paired outcomes on the assigned population, bounded qualification and
maintenance-inclusive cost. The final DataRobot study applies those criteria
to a concrete propensity-modeling workflow, distinguishing a useful component
from a complete causal estimator.
ending:
A useful assistant must help an economist ask a better question or examine
its evidence. Fluency is a different achievement. The discussion follows the
research task from business formulation and measurement to causal diagrams,
discovery, estimation and interpretation, before examining performance and cost.

title: What language models contribute to causal knowledge
opening:
Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} gives the principal recommendation for language
assistance. This chapter develops its evidential basis. It first distinguishes
knowledge, formal reasoning, mechanism proposals and workflow support, then
asks how published evaluations transfer to a banking decision. Exact examples
show how task mixtures, shared errors and unresolved causal models can change
that decision. The final comparisons examine consistency judges, orchestration,
literature extraction and the
ending:
The resulting recommendation is to test bounded roles against deterministic,
supervised and formal alternatives on the same complete requests. Retain
conflicts, refusal and operational failure, and price the review work needed
to obtain a defensible result. Before any of those comparisons can be designed,
the banking question itself must be explicit. The next chapter develops that
translation, including population weights, intervention definitions and the
information available at the decision time.

title: Translating a banking decision into a causal question
opening:
The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information
time. Incentive and servicing examples expose common substitutions; a
literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commi
ending:
Useful assistance records those distinctions, exposes what is unresolved and
preserves the evidence behind each accepted commitment. The subsequent formal
analysis then addresses the declared target under stated assumptions. The
next chapter applies this discipline to deposit pricing, arrears servicing,
underwriting and branch campaigns before developing their measurement and
monetary consequences.

title: Four banking translations before formal causal analysis
opening:
The four applications first distinguish plausible business questions before
choosing their formal targets. The remainder develops what those translations
must preserve: monetary units and repricing, measurement error and selective
notes, later servicing actions, and the applicant population. Studies of
linguistic measurements, variable construction, model representations and
clinical graph refinement then test the same discipline at more difficult
interfaces. Their different evidence cannot be c
ending:
The component comparisons make the same requirement operational. Perceived
politeness, an editing rule and a classifier label are different objects.
Compound phrases do not establish interaction effects, and improved graph or
image scores do not establish an intervention value. The next chapter turns
to the economic variables themselves: how to define their units, measurements,
relationships and clocks so that the formal question remains the one the bank
intends to answer.

title: Defining economic variables and measuring them
opening:
The application examples leave two connected questions: what the records
measure, and what the available evidence permits us to assert about them.
This chapter develops both. It begins with constructs, measurement error,
units and clocks; compares ontology and annotation tools; then examines
conflicting expert evidence and joint graph advice. The final Bayesian study
shows why response frequencies and accepted graph probabilities must remain
distinct. Each step asks what new information an assis
ending:
The practical output is a documented set of definitions and restrictions,
with unresolved alternatives and the information needed to distinguish them.
Deterministic dictionaries, human evidence review, soft-prior sensitivity and
formal graph calculations remain substantive alternatives to additional model
calls. The next chapter develops the diagrams and disagreement review that
consume these definitions, preserving their scientific and measurement limits.
\label{exec18:bayesian-advice-end}

title: Variables, diagrams and justified disagreement
opening:
The preceding chapter established what definitions and fallible evidence can
contribute. Here those objects enter a reviewable diagram. The argument first
separates graph classes, premises and retrieval outcomes, then develops exact
proxy, collider, clock and disagreement examples. The ontology comparison
connects the diagram to implementable treatment versions and source records.
The final restrictions study follows a premise through both graph and effect
sets, showing why a smaller graph class
ending:
The useful assistant therefore preserves alternative definitions and graphs,
explains which premises drive each result, and directs review toward
consequential disagreements. Formal methods, deterministic semantic checks and
human evidence review remain explicit alternatives or components. The next
chapter studies language assistance inside discovery procedures, where the
same distinctions must survive statistical tests, graph search and uncertainty
reporting.
\label{exec13:restriction-development-end}

title: Language assistance, causal discovery and uncertainty
opening:
This chapter follows a graph suggestion through the operations that could
make it useful for a decision. The opening comparison separates linguistic
knowledge from observations and interventions. The subsequent studies develop
information bounds, numerical alternatives, search failures, expert evidence
and executable graph contracts. Temporal and latent-variable examples then
show what those operations cannot determine from the supplied information.
The final identification study asks whether th
ending:
A defensible proposal therefore preserves the target and clock, compares
against numerical and expert alternatives, and carries semantic failures and
uncertainty through to the decision. Source-level repairs can make a tool's
behavior more faithful to its contract; they cannot create an identifying
observation. Where the remaining alternatives imply different actions, the
next question is which feasible experiment could distinguish them at worthwhile
cost. That is the subject of the next chapter.
\label{exec14:llm-identification-end}

title: Choosing the next experiment: information, decisions and agent limits
opening:
An agent that proposes a plausible causal diagram has not yet answered the
bank's next question: which additional observation could change a worthwhile
decision? A diagram may contain a dozen unresolved arrows, although only one
uncertainty affects whether a particular retention offer should be deployed.
Conversely, an apparently stable effect estimate can conceal a decisive
measurement or selection problem. Experiment selection therefore connects
problem formulation, causal discovery and invest
ending:
ainty that public and generated
evidence cannot settle. Its proposal should state which deployment decision
could change, the feasible observation law, the expected reduction in loss,
and the complete cost of obtaining that information. If candidate models
remain observationally equivalent under every permitted acquisition, the
appropriate result may be a restricted recommendation or abstention. An
agent adds value by recognizing that limit and specifying the missing
measurement or intervention, rather than by presenting another confident
causal narrative.
\label{exec13:active-experiments-end}

title: Assistance from research design to interpretation
opening:
The discovery and experiment-design arguments now enter a complete analytical
workflow. This chapter begins with the target and its handoffs, then develops
servicing, branch-rollout and observation examples. Their estimation errors
and policy-version distinctions give concrete tests for the architectural
comparison that follows. The final studies examine data preparation,
validation and reporting, so that a successful operation can be distinguished
from an answer to the bank's original question.
ending:
The proposed controller should preserve the question, unresolved premises and
evidence through those operations, with deterministic checks wherever their
conditions can be made explicit. Its advantage over a structured analyst
workflow remains an empirical question about usable answers and complete
review cost. The next chapter compares the tools that could implement this
restricted role, including the source, rights and execution obligations that
a plausible architecture alone cannot settle.
\label{exec14:estimation-validation-end}

title: Choosing tools for an accountable research assistant
opening:
The workflow comparison becomes a component decision here. The opening
frameworks and historical local controller establish the initial boundary.
The subsequent studies test evaluation, memory, information exchange, code
assistance and scientific reasoning against that boundary. Broader framework
and backend profiles then lead into their detailed parsing, validation, retry
and recovery paths. The question throughout is which useful operation can
be admitted without changing the causal object or
ending:
The initial investment is therefore a bounded comparison against the existing
controller and a structured analyst workflow. A selected original client or
framework needs its own exact environment and behavioral qualification. No
source profile supplies causal truth, a universal performance ranking or bank
acceptance. The following synthesis draws together the assistance and
implementation choices while retaining those limits.

title: Assistance and implementation choices
opening:
The preceding comparison establishes the component choices. This chapter
returns to the operation boundary that makes those choices useful: a
directional suggestion, a reviewed request and a qualified result are
different objects. The pairwise example makes the distinction concrete;
the remaining argument follows it through language boundaries, matched
qualification and commercial alternatives.
ending:
The immediate engineering requirements are nevertheless concrete. Preserve
scientific targets and uncertainty objects, expose method-specific unsupported
states, qualify language boundaries, and evaluate whole workflows under
declared assumptions. These requirements address defects that would otherwise
be hidden by a superficially uniform API. Completing the wider software
survey, commercial comparison and bank qualification requires additional
primary sources and trials; this selected review supplies evidence and
testable integration choices for that work.

title: Reporting causal results and monitoring their continued applicability
opening:
A servicing manager needs to know whether a contact policy improves thirty-day
net recovery, which accounts the conclusion concerns, and what could make it
inapplicable next month. A fluent explanation is useful only if it preserves the
answer supplied by the scientific analysis. A point estimate must not emerge
from a set of unresolved possibilities; a failed retrieval must not become
evidence that an assumption is false; and a successful replay must not certify
that a customer's information wa
ending:
The bounded survey leaves three candidate areas outside its inspected evidence:
a broad safety review, marketing context graphs, and traceable agents in
bioinformatics. Their technical claims require original-text and version review.
The proposed public and generated comparison can nevertheless proceed. It can
establish faithful handling of declared evidence and known cases; bank assignment
truth, general causal identification, selective calibration and useful
institutional monitoring remain separate questions.
\citep{exec16_report_contract}
\label{exec16:reporting-end}

title: Evaluating causal assistance without changing the question
opening: The question throughout this chapter is whether assistance preserves a banking decision while improving its resolution at an acceptable cost. The opening defines the comparison; the coverage screen and prospective experiment then show what a finite evaluation could establish. The source studies test the reference answers, exposure history, adjudication and scoring rules on which that experiment would rely. Finally, the evaluator, memory and toolkit comparisons follow those requirements into a wo
ending: erated problems with independent references, compare declared information and resource budgets, retain all assigned outcomes, and evaluate decision loss alongside availability and conditional accuracy. Choose the sample size from the particular claims and plausible effect margins, not from a convenient collection. A live comparison then addresses the remaining translation and review costs; an institutional study addresses the bank-specific assignment, transfer and monetary questions. Each stage can justify the next without borrowing a guarantee from a different target, score or software layer.

title: Comparing assistance with credible alternatives
opening:
An assistant should be judged against the work an analyst could already
do. Evaluation therefore needs simple baselines, tasks with defensible answers,
and a record of unresolved cases and correction costs. The following studies
ask what benchmarks, retrieval, code generation and simulated populations can
establish about that comparison.
ending:
The analyst should be able to follow the same study from source records
to the financial conclusion. A research library, a command-line tool and an
assistant using the Model Context Protocol are alternative ways to conduct that
study. Their design follows from the population, timing, intervention and
uncertainty established in the preceding parts.

title: Keeping the economic question intact across methods
opening: An analysis remains the same analysis only if its population, intervention, information and uncertainty survive each computational step. This chapter first develops that requirement for coordinates, graph classes and sets. It then examines the evidence from local custody, recovery and interface trials, before comparing restricted Python identification, Java discovery and R/native forest routes. Each route has a different scientific domain. Their common representation makes those domains visible;
ending: s beyond the estimator. A coordinate permutation, rounding at an integer boundary, a changed context, corrupt replay or incomplete publication can alter or conceal the scientific result. The observed refusals and successful recoveries establish particular behavior; the descriptor, input-access and error-classification findings identify repairs still needed for those versions. The next service design must carry both kinds of evidence forward. Its value is that a caller can tell what was computed, under which assumptions, what remains uncertain and which next action could resolve the limitation.

title: The library, command line and MCP service
opening:
A servicing analyst asks whether an offer would improve the next twelve
months' net value for accounts eligible today. A notebook, a scheduled command
and an agent can all transmit this question. They should receive the same
conditional answer when they submit the same declaration, inputs and method.
They should also retain the same unresolved assumptions. A successful call
which replaces the target population, changes the sign or drops an unbounded
component of an uncertainty set has failed as
ending:
and inspect the stored and exported objects, not merely the
screen caption. The finite reference already makes specific decoding and
interpretation errors reproducible. Completing an actual client would add
full schema validation, bounded parser resources, live transport ordering,
artifact retrieval, custody policy and launch-environment trials. These are
known engineering steps justified by the proposal. They remain separate
from expensive bank experiments, which should follow only after the
prototype demonstrates useful preservation of the scientific question.
\label{exec17:i2-admission-end}

title: Using the analysis in other research applications
opening: A useful connection joins a consumer's decision to a provider's scientific result without changing either. The cases here follow four banking journeys: funding value, sequential servicing, discovery ambiguity and trustworthy observations. Population transport and cash-flow composition then show why correct individual exchanges may still fail when combined. The resulting comparison favors a reviewed manual exchange as the baseline and automation only where the same scientific output can be preser
ending:
The reusable contribution is the target-preserving workflow, including its
failure states. The exact examples are reproducible with
\path{tools/workspace_examples_20261013.py}, using a fresh output path; they
require only the Python standard library and execute no sibling code~\citep{exec13_i3_examples}. They demonstrate why the proposed interfaces need
